# Native DEXPI 2.0.1 documents

pyDEXPI's classes are DEXPI 2.0.1. Everything else under `data/` is a DEXPI 2.0 document (or a
Proteus file) that pyDEXPI reads through its 2.0 -> 2.0.1 conversion, so this directory holds the
documents that need no conversion at all:

| File | What it is | Origin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reference_pid.xml` | The DEXPI 2.0.1 specification's reference P&ID | Vendored **byte-identical** from the release (below) |
| `synthetic_process.xml`, `synthetic_process.json` | A small DEXPI 2.0.1 process model, in both formats | Generated by `make_synthetic_process.py` |
| `make_synthetic_process.py` | The generator of the two files above | pyDEXPI |

All three documents are in the corpus sweep (`tests/test_roundtrip/test_corpus.py`).

## `reference_pid.xml`: the DEXPI 2.0.1 reference P&ID

| | |
|---|---|
| Upstream | <https://gitlab.com/dexpi/Specification> |
| Release | <https://gitlab.com/dexpi/Specification/-/releases/V2.0.1> |

| Upstream path | `src/documentation/_static/reference_pid.xml` (the file the specification's appendix "Reference P&ID" links) |
| Downloaded from | <https://gitlab.com/dexpi/Specification/-/raw/eef0f0c6e8edfe84582e7a45d109c396bdc544f8/src/documentation/_static/reference_pid.xml> |
| Bytes | 1,481,865 |

The specification states that it "is provided by the DEXPI Initiative under the terms of the
Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC BY 4.0)"
(`src/documentation/index.rst` at the tag); this file is part of it. `NOTICE` carries the same
attribution for the distribution.

**Do not reformat, re-indent or re-serialize it.** `.gitattributes` marks it `-text`, so a
Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf` cannot rewrite its line endings, and
`test_reference_pid_2_0_1.py::test_the_vendored_file_is_byte_identical_to_the_release` checks the
hash above. To re-verify, download the URL above and compare the SHA-256.

### Why there are two reference P&IDs

`data/reference_pid.xml` (with its JSON twin) is the DEXPI **2.0** reference P&ID and stays as it
is. It is the real-world input of the 2.0 -> 2.0.1 conversion, and hundreds of tests pin its ids,
tags and drawing; replacing it would move those pins for reasons unrelated to 2.0.1. This file is
what the same drawing looks like as a native 2.0.1 document, and pyDEXPI reads it without
converting anything: a strict load registers no entry at all, `validate()` reports no issue, and
XML and JSON round trips are exact.

Measured against pyDEXPI's 2.0 copy loaded through the conversion, the two hold the same 1,612
objects and the same 298 document ids, and differ in exactly these places
(`tests/test_roundtrip/test_reference_pid_2_0_1.py` pins each one):

- the `<Import>` URIs name `models/2.0.1` instead of `models/2.0.0`;
- the 19 nozzles are typed with the classes 2.0.1 added: 17 `ProcessNozzle`, one
  `InstrumentNozzle` (`Nozzle17`) and one `AccessNozzle` (`Nozzle19`), where 2.0 has `Nozzle`;
  every one of the 71 references to a nozzle still names its counterpart;
- the `EngineeringModel` carries an `ExportDateTime`, `2026-09-30T09:00:00`; a pyDEXPI export
  keeps it, as it keeps every set field (`pydexpi.attribution` never overwrites);
- the eight `Shape`s whose `SymbolRegistrationNumber` the 2.0 example left out carry real ones
  (`CONTROLLED_ACTUATOR_SHAPE`, `T_TYPE_CONNECTION_SHAPE`, ...), where pyDEXPI's copy has the
  placeholder `MISSING_IN_ORIGINAL_EXAMPLE_FILE`;
- in the text only: five empty strings are `<String></String>` rather than `<String/>`, and the
  file ends with a newline.

## `synthetic_process.*`: a native DEXPI 2.0.1 process model

No public DEXPI 2.0.1 process model exists yet; the three in `data/` (the CO2 terminal, Tennessee
Eastman, the bpmn2dexpi export) are DEXPI 2.0. This one is synthetic: a feed, a distillation
column and a bottom-product sink, built with pyDEXPI's generated classes so that it holds one of
each 2.0.1 process construct the real files lack:

- a `ProcessStepDetail` (the column's feed tray, `ContactingOnTray`) owning a port;
- an `InstrumentationActivity` (`MeasuringProcessVariable` PT-101) owning two `informationPorts`,
  and two `InformationFlow`s through it;
- a delegated port pair: the stripping section's feed port delegates the column's feed port, with
  `superReference` / `subReference` both ways and the column's feed stream as its
  `connectorReference`. `SubReference` is written as a reference
  (`<References property="SubReference">`), where the specification declares a composition: that
  is pyDEXPI's `PORT-SUBREFERENCE` deviation (`AGENTS.md`), since the delegate is already owned by
  its sub-step's `ports`;
- `Stream`s between `MaterialPort`s, every port and the feed tray performing `Role`s owned by
  `ProcessModel.roles`, each named from the specification's list for its class (the tray performs
  `Monitored`, a `ContactingOnTray` name);
- a `MaterialTemplate` whose `ListOfMaterialComponents` orders three components (water, ethanol,
  methanol) in an order that is not that of their ids;
- a `MaterialState` owning two `phases` and a `state`, each a `MaterialStateType` carrying its
  total `massFlow` and composing a `Composition` with `massFractions` (a `PhysicalQuantityVector`
  in `RatioUnit.Percent`, summing to 100) and `massFlow` as one quantity per component in the
  template's order (the specification's "vector of mass flow rates for each component");
- every property the specification declares `Undefined | X` with multiplicity 1..1 that its
  objects carry, set to a value or to an explicit `Undefined` (`QualifiedValue.DisplayText`, the
  `Label` of every `ProcessConnection`, `ProcessStepDetail` and activity, the `EngineeringModel`'s
  originating system). pyDEXPI's classes make these twelve properties optional, so neither
  construction nor `validate()` notices one left out; `REQUIRED_UNDEFINABLE` in the
  generator lists them, and a test checks the fixture against it;
- a diagram whose `RepresentationGroup`s anchor `PortNodePosition`s on the ports, with
  `ConnectorLine`s between them.

Every object has an explicit id, so the generator always builds the same model.
`tests/test_roundtrip/test_synthetic_process_2_0_1.py` pins that the committed files are what it
builds, that both load strictly and validate without an issue, that XML and JSON round trips are
exact, and that the component order and the fraction values survive every round trip. A strict
load registers one WARNING per cut of the required `Port` <-> `ProcessConnection` cycle, which
every process document contains, and nothing else.

To change it, edit `make_synthetic_process.py` and regenerate both files from anywhere:

```bash
python data/dexpi_2_0_1/make_synthetic_process.py
```

The XML's first line names the pyDEXPI version that wrote it; nothing else depends on the
environment.

The synthetic fixture is pyDEXPI's own work, under the repository's licence.
